implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: a hint issued to the memory system naming an address, a read/write flag, and a locality level saying how long the data will be reused. The discipline: (1) confirm with counters that the workload is latency-bound, not compute-bound; (2) compute the address far enough ahead for the fetch to overlap real work - typically one pointer-load of lookahead in a chase, or one loop iteration in a strided loop; (3) prefetch only what will be used, and no more than the fill buffers can track; (4) prefer the lowest cache level that will still hold the data. Below the same idea sit the OS analogues - readahead and MADV_WILLNEED for pages - and the branch hint, which predicts instead of fetches. Every hint is advisory: measure, because the hardware and compiler may both ignore it.
idiom_name: explicit prefetch hint (address + read/write + locality), the OS analogue readahead/MADV_WILLNEED, and the branch hint
code_sketch:
# pointer chase: the address of the NEXT node is not known until the
# current one is read, so prefetch one level ahead from the pointer we just loaded
for step in range(steps):
    node = node.next              # load the pointer
    prefetch_read(node, locality=L3)  # hint: fetch the node body (or the child pointer)
    total += node.value           # the stall here is now overlapped

# strided loop: prefetch the next row/iteration
for i in range(n):
    prefetch_read(&a[(i + PREFETCH_DISTANCE) * stride], locality=L2)
    consume(a[i * stride])

# OS analogue: fault the region in before the latency-sensitive section
madvise(region, len, MADV_WILLNEED)   # or posix_fadvise(fd, 0, len, POSIX_FADV_WILLNEED)
pitfalls: Too close: the line has not arrived; too far: it is evicted. The distance is a tuning parameter measured on the target part.
Speculative prefetch past the fill buffers causes drops or stalls, and on strong-reliability CPUs an actual stall with no benefit.
A prefetch inside a vectorisable inner loop inhibits vectorisation - hoist it out.
It is a hint: the compiler may remove it and the CPU may drop it, so deleting one as cleanup can cost the latency it hid.
